title: Sell Mineral Rights in Greenbrier, AR
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Greenbrier, AR | Faulkner County
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Greenbrier, Arkansas in core Faulkner County? We evaluate legacy Fayetteville Shale interests and make a straightforward cash offer.
heroLead: Greenbrier sits in growing northern Faulkner County, inside the core of the Fayetteville Shale, where residential growth has increasingly overlapped with legacy gas production.
intro: Greenbrier has grown steadily as Conway's metro area has expanded northward, and some of the land here that once held straightforward rural mineral interests is now subdivided for housing. As with Conway itself, that growth doesn't erase the mineral estate, but it does mean owners should confirm exactly what they hold before assuming a surface sale carried the minerals along with it.

sections.heading: Core Fayetteville Shale drilling history
paragraphs: Greenbrier and the surrounding sections were part of the dense Faulkner County drilling activity during the play's boom years. Well results here were generally strong relative to the rest of the play, though current production reflects more than a decade of decline since.

sections.heading: Residential growth and mineral severance
paragraphs: As Greenbrier has grown, land that was once a single rural tract has sometimes been split into residential lots, and the treatment of mineral rights in those subdivisions varies. Some developers reserved minerals, others let them pass with the lots. We check your specific deed chain to confirm which applies to you.
This is worth resolving before assuming you still hold the same mineral interest your family originally had on the land.

sections.heading: Pricing off current production, not the boom-years peak
paragraphs: As with the rest of Faulkner County, we price Greenbrier-area interests using current decline-adjusted production data rather than the well's original output when it was first drilled.

faqs.question: Our land near Greenbrier has been subdivided since our family originally owned it. Do we still have mineral rights?
faqs.answer: It depends on how minerals were handled in the subdivision deeds. We check your specific chain of title to confirm.

faqs.question: Was this part of Faulkner County heavily drilled during the Fayetteville Shale boom?
faqs.answer: Yes, northern Faulkner County including the Greenbrier area saw substantial drilling activity during the 2005 to 2012 period.

faqs.question: How is our interest priced given how much the well has declined?
faqs.answer: We use current production and decline trend, not the well's historical peak, to arrive at a value.

faqs.question: What if part of our Greenbrier-area tract was already leased to a developer for housing?
faqs.answer: A surface lease or sale for development doesn't necessarily affect the mineral estate. We check the specific deed language to confirm what, if anything, changed.

faqs.question: What if our Greenbrier property was subdivided and we're not sure which lot still carries the mineral rights?
faqs.answer: We can trace the subdivision deeds to identify exactly which lot, if any, retained the mineral estate, before pricing anything.
